Using the Terminal

1 Why use the terminal?

RNA-seq analysis happens on a remote computing cluster (Unity). The cluster does not have a graphical desktop — you interact with it entirely by typing commands into a terminal window.

This page covers the commands you will use most often. You do not need to memorize them. Refer back here whenever you need a reminder.

2 Open a terminal

On macOS: Open the Terminal app. You can find it in Applications → Utilities, or search for it with Spotlight (⌘ + Space, type “Terminal”).

On Windows: Open Windows Terminal, PowerShell, or install Git Bash.

On Linux: Open your terminal application.

3 Understanding file paths

A path describes where a file or folder is located. There are two types:

Absolute path — starts from the very top of the filesystem with /. It works the same no matter where you currently are.

/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/03_26_flut_yale_rnaseq

Relative path — starts from wherever you currently are. A . means “here” and .. means “one folder up”.

../results/multiqc_report.html
Tip

When in doubt, use absolute paths. They are harder to get wrong because they always point to the same place.

4 Where am I?

Print your current working directory:

pwd

Example output:

/home/kfloer_smith_edu

5 List files

List files in the current directory:

ls

Show more information, including file sizes:

ls -lh

Example output:

drwxr-xr-x  2 kfloer_smith_edu users  4.0K Jun  8 results/
-rw-r--r--  1 kfloer_smith_edu users  1.2K Jun  8 samplesheet.csv

The columns show: permissions, number of links, owner, group, size, date modified, name. Entries starting with d are directories; entries starting with - are files.

6 Change directories

Move into a folder:

cd results

Move up one folder:

cd ..

Move to your home directory (the shortcut ~ always means your home):

cd ~

Move to an absolute path:

cd /work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu

7 Make a new directory

Create a folder:

mkdir job-logs

Create a nested folder path all at once (the -p flag creates any missing parent folders):

mkdir -p ~/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs

8 Create and edit a text file with nano

nano is a simple terminal text editor. You will use it to write job scripts on Unity.

Open a new file (or open an existing one):

nano my-script.sh

This opens the file inside the terminal. You can type normally. At the bottom of the screen you will see shortcuts:

^O  Write Out (save)       ^X  Exit
^K  Cut line               ^U  Paste

The ^ symbol means Ctrl. So ^O means Ctrl + O.

To save: press Ctrl + O, then press Enter to confirm the filename.

To exit: press Ctrl + X.

Tip

If you accidentally start nano and want to leave without saving, press Ctrl + X and then type N when asked if you want to save.

9 Look at text files without editing

Print a whole file to the terminal:

cat samplesheet.csv

Show just the first 10 lines of a file:

head samplesheet.csv

Show just the last 10 lines:

tail samplesheet.csv

Watch a file update in real time (useful for watching log files as a job runs):

tail -f job-logs/nfcore-rnaseq-test.12345.out

Press Ctrl + C to stop watching.

10 Move, rename, and copy files

Move a file into a folder:

mv samplesheet.csv nf-core-demo/

Rename a file:

mv old_name.csv new_name.csv

Copy a file:

cp samplesheet.csv samplesheet_backup.csv

Copy an entire folder and everything inside it:

cp -r results/ results_backup/

11 Check disk usage

See how much space a file or folder is using:

du -sh results/

See how much space is left on the filesystem you are currently on:

df -h .

On Unity, you will use this to make sure you have not filled your scratch workspace.

12 Copy files between Unity and your laptop

scp copies files between your laptop and Unity. Run these commands from a terminal on your laptop (not from Unity).

Copy a file from Unity to your current folder on your laptop:

scp kfloer_smith_edu@unity.rc.umass.edu:/path/to/multiqc_report.html .

Copy a whole folder from Unity to your laptop:

scp -r kfloer_smith_edu@unity.rc.umass.edu:/path/to/results/ .

Copy a file from your laptop to Unity:

scp samplesheet.csv kfloer_smith_edu@unity.rc.umass.edu:/scratch4/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-demo/

The . at the end means “copy it here, into my current directory.”

Note

Replace kfloer_smith_edu with your own Unity username, and replace the paths with your actual paths.

13 Common commands at a glance

Goal Command
See where you are pwd
List files ls
List files with sizes ls -lh
Move into a folder cd folder_name
Move up one folder cd ..
Go to home directory cd ~
Create a folder mkdir folder_name
Create nested folders mkdir -p parent/child/grandchild
Create/edit a file nano file.txt
Print a file cat file.txt
Preview the start head file.txt
Preview the end tail file.txt
Watch a file live tail -f file.txt
Move or rename mv old new
Copy a file cp source destination
Copy a folder cp -r source/ destination/
Folder size du -sh folder/
Disk space left df -h .
Copy to/from server scp source destination

14 Tips for beginners

  • File and folder names are case-sensitive. Results and results are different.
  • Avoid spaces in file names — use underscores _ or hyphens - instead.
  • Press Tab to autocomplete a file or folder name. Press it twice to see all options.
  • Use the ↑ arrow key to scroll through previous commands.
  • Read error messages carefully — they usually tell you exactly what went wrong.
  • If a command seems to hang, press Ctrl + C to cancel it.
